== Proofs of the relationships in the map ==
{{Algebraic structures |Lattice}}

1. A [[Boolean algebra (structure)|boolean algebra]] is a [[complemented lattice|complemented]] [[distributive lattice]]. (def)

'''2'''. A boolean algebra is a [[heyting algebra]].<ref>Rutherford (1965), p.77.</ref>

3. A boolean algebra is [[orthocomplemented lattice|orthocomplemented]].<ref>Rutherford (1965), p.32-33.</ref>

4. A distributive orthocomplemented lattice is [[orthomodular lattice#Orthomodular lattices|orthomodular]].

'''5'''. A boolean algebra is orthomodular. (1,3,4)

'''6'''. An orthomodular lattice is orthocomplemented. (def)

'''7'''. An orthocomplemented lattice is complemented. (def)

'''8'''. A complemented lattice is bounded. (def)

'''9'''. An [[algebraic lattice]] is complete. (def)

'''10'''. A [[complete lattice]] is bounded.

'''11'''. A heyting algebra is bounded. (def)

'''12'''. A bounded lattice is a lattice. (def)

'''13'''. A heyting algebra is [[residuated lattice|residuated]].

'''14'''. A residuated lattice is a lattice. (def)

'''15'''. A distributive lattice is modular.<ref>Rutherford (1965), p.22.</ref>

16. A modular complemented lattice is relatively complemented.<ref>Rutherford (1965), p.31.</ref>

'''17'''. A boolean algebra is [[relatively complemented lattice|relatively complemented]]. (1,15,16)

'''18'''. A relatively complemented lattice is a lattice. (def)

'''19'''. A heyting algebra is distributive.<ref>Rutherford (1965), Th.25.1 p.74.</ref>

'''20'''. A [[totally ordered set]] is a distributive lattice.

'''21'''. A [[metric lattice]] is [[modular lattice|modular]].<ref>Rutherford (1965), Th.8.1 p.22.</ref>

'''22'''. A modular lattice is semi-modular.<ref>Rutherford (1965), p.87.</ref>

'''23'''. A [[projective lattice]] is modular.<ref>Rutherford (1965), p.94.</ref>

'''24'''. A projective lattice is geometric. (def)

'''25'''. A [[geometric lattice]] is semi-modular.<ref>Rutherford (1965), Th.32.1 p.92.</ref>

'''26'''. A semi-modular lattice is atomic.<ref>Rutherford (1965), p.89.</ref>{{Disputed inline|Content error|date=May 2017}}

'''27'''. An [[atomic (order theory)|atomic]] lattice is a lattice. (def)

'''28'''. A lattice is a semi-lattice. (def)

'''29'''. A [[semi-lattice]] is a [[partially ordered set]]. (def)
